replication.target_description: Reassurance seeking predicting ACT scores controlling for high school rank percentile and GPA; primary replication test, one-tailed p.

n.exclusions: Missing observed values (table Ns 53–59) were mean-imputed.
n.quote:
Fifty-nine Introduction to Psychology students from a large university in the midwestern United
States were recruited to participate in this study. ... The amount of missing data was small, so mean
imputation was used to account for missing data.

es.quote:
After controlling for high school rank percentile
and high school GPA, ACT scores were signiﬁcantly predicted by reassurance seeking (partial r =
−.23, p = .046).

p.quote:
After controlling for high school rank percentile
and high school GPA, ACT scores were signiﬁcantly predicted by reassurance seeking (partial r =
−.23, p = .046).

reported_success.quote: This pattern of results replicates the ﬁndings from Knoll et al. (2019).

notes: Published online 2020 copy. The primary adjusted ACT test matches the replication hypothesis. The zero-order r=.00 is a different test; extra adjustment for test/cognitive anxiety on p.6 yields partial r=−.14, p=.165. Authors qualify support under that stronger adjustment.
